_doc: Bilingual label data consumed by tools/build_discovery_catalog.py.
Every catalog point and every enum token must resolve to a label in BOTH
languages; this file supplies the side the evidence (APK English labels,
German reference bundle) does not provide. Translations are data, not
runtime behavior: the builder bakes them into the shipped catalog with
provenance 'translated'.
Rules used when authoring:
* HVAC domain terminology, matched to the register of the 208 verified
apk_label/bundle pairs already in the catalog (see _glossary).
* Technical machine symbols (catalog.is_technical_name) are NEVER
translated - the builder keeps them verbatim in both languages, so
they have no entry here.
* Units, numbers and proper nouns (OCHSNER, Climatix, DHW, EVU, JAZ)
stay intact; numeric/identity labels (baud rates, UTC offsets) map to
themselves explicitly so the audit can tell 'reviewed identity' from
'missing'.
* names_en_to_de:   APK-label English point name  -> German display name
* names_de_to_en:   bundle German point name      -> English display name
* enum_shared_en_to_de: normalized enum token -> German label, translating
the shared APK-resource English label (enum_token_labels.en) for that
token. Shared application is justified exactly like the EN map: it is
derived from the token-keyed APK resources, not from point-specific
bundle evidence.
* enum_labels_de_to_en: exact German enum label (from a point's
bundle-joined enum_labels_de) -> English label; applied per point, so a
point-specific German label never relabels another point.
* enum_token_labels_both: normalized token -> {en, de} for tokens that
have NO label evidence on either side but whose meaning is unambiguous
from the token itself; applied as shared labels in both languages.
